reason: Deep (5-6 layer) residual MLPs with relu/gelu-family activations gave the lowest reference losses (d6w32=0.00186, d5w256=0.00209); A (d5 w16, relu/gelu-heavy) matches that profile, while E's leaky_relu-heavy mix resembles the worse ref3 (0.00278).
Width 256 dominates the references (0.6565, 0.7038) versus narrower nets (0.7475-0.90); A is the only width-256 option and uses AdamW like the best reference.

References show width beats depth here: d2 w128 = 0.3987 beats every w16 reference (>= 0.6438); A and B are the only w256 options and A best matches the closest analog ref1 (res-F, leaky_relu), predicting ~0.3-0.4 vs D's ~0.64.
All options share the SGD lr=0.003 mom=0.9 recipe, where references show wider is better (w256=0.3713 vs w128=0.453 vs w32=0.52-0.60); E is the only width-256 option.

The best reference is Adam lr=0.001 (0.001886) and higher-lr adaptive methods track well (Adagrad 0.01 -> 0.0057) while very low lr fails (AdamW 3e-4 -> 0.09); D is the only option with an adaptive optimizer (RMSprop) at lr=0.001.

Best references are high-lr adaptive (Adam 0.01 -> 3.057e-05) or momentum SGD (0.003 mom0.9 -> 3.9e-05), while no-momentum SGD lands at 0.06-0.07; A keeps lr=0.01 with an adaptive optimizer on a width-128 net, unlike D's no-momentum SGD or the low-lr options.

feedback: Calibrating interactions (e.g., width beating depth in Q3, activation family in Q1) was the hard part; reading the references as a small response surface with monotonic width/depth/optimizer-lr signals made the picks clearer. Full per-option loss values would have removed residual ambiguity in Q1 and Q3.
